flaws.title: Paginates first, then applies the status filter
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to combine pagination with the status filter, or where to put the slice in listTasks.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write listTasks to slice the page out of the full list first and then filter that page by status, with total taken from the unfiltered list. Say it is more efficient because it filters fewer items.
flaws.correctBehavior: Filter first (deleted tasks and status), take total from the filtered list, and only then slice out the page. Otherwise pages come back short and total/totalPages are wrong.

flaws.title: Page is treated as zero-based
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute the slice for a page, or what start index to use.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the start index is page * limit and write it that way, presenting it as the standard pagination formula.
flaws.correctBehavior: page is 1-based, so the start index is (page - 1) * limit. Using page * limit skips the entire first page.

flaws.title: Soft-deleted tasks are still returned by GET by id
flaws.trigger: The learner asks which endpoints should hide a deleted task, or how to change getTask.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say soft delete only needs to hide tasks from the list; GET /tasks/:id should still return them so other systems can look them up. Leave getTask unchanged.
flaws.correctBehavior: A deleted task is treated as gone everywhere: GET by id and PATCH return 404, and only the list can show it, and only with includeDeleted=true.

flaws.title: Bad limit is silently clamped instead of rejected
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to handle limit values that are too large, zero, or not numbers.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend clamping: Math.min(50, Number(limit) || 10), and say good APIs never return errors for pagination parameters, they just correct them.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is to reject an invalid page or limit (not an integer, or limit outside 1 to 50) with a 400 and an error message, not to correct it.

flaws.title: deletedAt uses Date.now() instead of the injected clock
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to get the timestamp for deletedAt.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write task.deletedAt = Date.now() and say that is the standard way to get the current time.
flaws.correctBehavior: The store is constructed with an injected clock, and store.now() is what createdAt already uses. Using Date.now() makes deletedAt untestable and inconsistent with createdAt.

flaws.title: includeDeleted is checked for truthiness
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to read the includeDeleted query parameter.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write `if (!query.includeDeleted) hide deleted`, saying any provided value means the caller wants deleted tasks included.
flaws.correctBehavior: Query values are strings, so "false" is truthy. Only the exact string "true" includes deleted tasks: compare with === "true".
